summary.what_changed: The orchestrator now vendors the plugin directory (passed to the Claude CLI via --plugin-dir) to a location outside the git worktree for page-author dispatches. It no longer uses --permission-mode auto to get past the 'sensitive file' write gate on plugin-dir paths. Page writes therefore no longer depend on a server-side classifier verdict. A new test file, tests/orchestrator/test_plugin_dir_write_denial.py, covers the write-denial scenario.
summary.why: CCE-188 fixed the 100% 'sensitive file' write denials by switching to --permission-mode auto. That mode makes a server-side safety classifier approve each write. On nightly 36241035222 (2026-09-26) the classifier returned no verdict. All ten page-author dispatches failed, zero pages were authored, the baseline stayed frozen at 1718883f, and PR #298 was left open as a partial run. Moving the plugin directory outside the worktree removes the sensitive-file trigger without needing a third party to rule on each write.

summary.what_changed: The fact-checker output schema no longer requires the `ok` field. The orchestrator's fact-checker consumer reads only `verdict` and `findings`, so an answer that omits `ok` is now accepted instead of being recorded as `fact_checker_unavailable`. The change updates `agents/schemas/fact_checker.schema.json` and the canonical schema block in `agents/fact-checker.md` together. It also updates the typed view in `scripts/contracts.py`. It adds tests, including a fixture of the real nightly response that omitted `ok`.
summary.why: On nightly run 36741357748, one of 16 fact-checker dispatches returned a complete answer with `verdict` and `findings` but no `ok`. The schema listed `ok` as required, so the run reported a schema failure and went blind, and auto-merge was skipped as `blind_run`. The orchestrator never reads `ok`. This is the same class as CCE-180 and CCE-125: a schema stricter than its consumer turns a usable answer into a handled failure.

summary.what_changed: The orchestrator now bounds the source-collector's input window before dispatching it, instead of capping only after the collector has already emitted output. The collector gets a window bound plus metadata anchors, so a baseline far behind no longer produces an output the collector can't fit. The source-collector agent contract was updated to match. Tests cover the window bound and the blind/degraded classification coverage audit.
summary.why: CCE-169's window cap ran after the collector dispatch. With a very wide window (ADIS run 37493982560: 173 in-window PRs, only 12 returned), the collector invented an uncontracted `output_size_limit` error. That error fell into the generic `sources.get("error")` branch and was recorded as blind. A blind run exits non-zero, skips auto-merge and freezes the watermark. The window then widened each night, so every later run failed the same way.

doc_targets.notes: Describe the collector window bound applied at dispatch, before the CCE-169 admission cap, and the metadata anchors.
